newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD says mulling stronger telecom ties with TT Net.
newsitem.headline: KDD says mulling stronger telecom ties with TT Net.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd said on Thursday that it and affiliates of electric power utilities are considering strengthening their ties by offering joint telecommunications services.
"We are exploring ways to expand our telecom business ties," KDD president Tadashi Nishimoto told a news conference.
Asked about possible areas of future cooperation in telecoms services, he cited development and jointly offering seamless regional-to-international services.
KDD is not considering acquiring shares in the firms for now, Nishimoto said.

The nine affiliates of electric power utilities, including Tokyo Telecommunication Network Co (TT Net), had already agreed to connect their on-land optical fibre networks with KDD's planned underseas fibre optic cable by 1999.
The nine companies have offered leased-line services throughout Japan using their parent companies' optic fibre networks.
TT Net, an affiliate of Tokyo Electric Power Co, plans to offer a low-cost city-call service in Tokyo this year.
KDD's Nishimoto also nearly half the planned capacity of its undersea cable would be eventually sold to other telecom carriers, reducing the overall cost of the move.
KDD earlier announced that it would construct an undersea optic fibre cable looping around Japan's three islands by 1999 at a total construction cost of 130 billion yen.
